name: org.machanism.machai:gw-maven-plugin
description: GW Maven Plugin is the Maven adapter for the Machai Ghostwriter application. It brings guided AI-assisted file processing into Maven-based projects so teams can analyze, update, and maintain source code, tests, documentation, site content, configuration, and other project files from the same build-oriented workflow. The plugin implements Maven goals for guidance-driven processing and act-driven processing: gw:gw scans selected files for @guidance comments, gw:act applies a reusable act name or a direct user prompt, and gw:gw-per-module and gw:act-per-module run the corresponding workflows in Maven reactor module context. Aggregator goals can run in normal Maven projects, multi-module projects, or directories without a pom.xml, while per-module goals require a Maven project. The plugin resolves Maven project, session, reactor, settings, scan paths, exclusions, instructions, model selection, and provider credentials, then delegates work to Machai Ghostwriter processors. It supports Maven settings.xml server credentials for GenAI providers, optional Ghostwriter configuration files, debug logging via SLF4J SimpleLogger properties, parallel execution patterns, and Java class-introspection function tools that can find classes and inspect reflective metadata. It is primarily useful for documentation automation, guided file processing, AI-assisted project maintenance, repeatable repository workflows, Maven plugin integration, and GenAI-enabled developer automation.

usageContext: Run from the Maven command line to process project files containing @guidance comments
Run from Maven as gw:act to apply a predefined act or direct prompt to selected project content
Run in multi-module Maven builds with aggregator goals or Maven reactor per-module goals
Use in documentation maintenance workflows for source, tests, site markdown, configuration, and other repository files
Use with GenAI provider credentials stored in Maven settings.xml or Ghostwriter configuration files
Use class-introspection function tools to support AI workflows that need Java API awareness

constructors.description: Creates the Maven goal implementation for gw:gw. Maven constructs this mojo when the guidance-processing goal is invoked. The goal builds the effective Ghostwriter processor configuration, resolves project layout information when Maven project context exists, configures non-recursive and parallel execution behavior, and scans files for @guidance comments.

examples.description: Installs and invokes the plugin directly by fully qualified Maven coordinates without adding it to the build. The command configures the scan path to src/site and excludes target and node_modules while running guidance-driven processing. Maven constructs org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.GWMojo internally.

constructors.description: Creates the Maven goal implementation for gw:act. Maven constructs this mojo when the act-processing goal is invoked. The goal resolves a predefined act name, an act plus additional prompt text, or a direct prompt beginning with >, then configures an ActProcessor and scans the selected project documents.

examples.description: Runs the act goal directly from Maven coordinates. Maven downloads the plugin if needed, constructs org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.ActMojo, loads the review act, and applies it to files under src/main/java.

constructors.description: Creates function-tool integrations backed by a Maven project classpath. The tool scans the project compile classpath plus main and test output directories so AI-assisted processing can find classes and retrieve structured reflective metadata.

examples.snippet:
org.apache.maven.project.MavenProject project = new org.apache.maven.project.MavenProject();
org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools tools = new org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools(project);
examples.description: Programmatic construction for advanced integrations or tests. In normal plugin usage, the Maven mojo registers these tools automatically when a MavenProject is available.

features.name: Guidance-driven file processing
features.description: Runs the gw:gw Maven goal. The goal creates and configures a GuidanceProcessor, resolves Maven project layout and reactor context, applies path, model, instructions, excludes, interactive settings, and credentials, then scans selected files for Ghostwriter @guidance comments. It is designed for repeatable AI-assisted maintenance of all project file types, not only Java source code.

examples.description: After configuring the plugin in pom.xml, this command scans Maven site markdown files, reads additional instructions from docs/guidance.md, excludes generated output, and updates files according to embedded @guidance comments.

features.name: Act execution
features.description: Runs the gw:act Maven goal. The goal resolves a predefined act or direct prompt, configures an ActProcessor, and applies the selected task to project files. A prompt-only act must begin with >, while a predefined act can be passed as a name and may include additional prompt text after the act name.

examples.snippet:
mvn gw:act -Dgw.act=review -Dgw.path=src/main/java
mvn gw:act -Dgw.act=">Update the README and Maven site pages for the latest plugin behavior"
examples.description: The first command runs the predefined review act on Java sources. The second command uses a direct prompt, identified by the leading > character, to update documentation-oriented files selected by the configured scan path.

features.name: Per-module guidance processing
features.description: Runs the gw:gw-per-module goal once per Maven reactor module. Maven determines module execution order using the standard reactor dependency graph. The mojo reuses shared scanning and GenAI configuration from AbstractGWMojo and binds Maven-specific project layout metadata for each processed module.

examples.description: Processes each module in a reactor build through Maven's per-module execution model, scanning each module's site content with shared instructions.

features.name: Find Java classes for AI workflows
features.description: Finds fully qualified class names whose simple class names match a regular expression. The search is resolved against class metadata cached for a Maven project base directory. It supports AI workflows that need to discover candidate classes before inspecting detailed API metadata.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools tools = new org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools(project);
java.util.List<java.lang.String> classes = tools.findClass(".*Mojo", project.getBasedir());
examples.description: Programmatic use of the class-discovery function to find Maven mojo classes by simple-name regular expression. In normal Ghostwriter processing, this function is exposed to the AI workflow as a function tool.

features.name: Inspect Java class metadata
features.signature: public java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object> org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools.getClassInfo(java.lang.String className, java.io.File projectDir) throws java.lang.ClassNotFoundException
features.description: Returns reflective information for a fully qualified Java class. The resulting map may include modifiers, superclass, interfaces, non-private fields, constructors, non-private methods, annotations, the class path, source path, and dependency artifact coordinates. This helps AI documentation and analysis tasks ground generated content in the actual project or dependency classpath.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools tools = new org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.tools.ClassFunctionalTools(project);
java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object> info = tools.getClassInfo("org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.GWMojo", project.getBasedir());
examples.description: Retrieves structured metadata for the fully qualified org.machanism.machai.gw.maven.GWMojo class, including public and protected API details useful for generated documentation.

customizations.name: gw.model
customizations.description: Selects the provider/model identifier passed to the Ghostwriter workflow, for example CodeMie:gpt-5.6-terra-2026-07-09 or another configured provider model.

examples.description: Overrides the model for one Maven invocation.

customizations.name: genai.serverId
customizations.description: Specifies the Maven settings.xml server id used to load GenAI provider credentials and custom configuration values such as username, password, and provider-specific XML entries.

examples.description: Configures provider credentials in Maven settings.xml and references them from the command line without exposing secrets directly in the command.

customizations.name: gw.path
customizations.description: Selects the file, directory, glob, or supported pattern to scan. This allows workflows to focus on source code, tests, documentation, Maven site content, or other repository areas.

examples.description: Runs an act against Maven site markdown documentation rather than the entire project.

examples.title: Install and run guidance processing with direct Maven coordinates
steps: Ensure a JDK and Maven are installed and available on PATH.
Create or select project files that contain @guidance comments describing the desired updates.
Configure GenAI provider credentials in Maven settings.xml or through the Ghostwriter configuration used by your environment.
Run the plugin by fully qualified Maven coordinates.
examples.description: This scenario downloads the plugin from Maven repositories if needed and invokes gw:gw without requiring a plugin entry in pom.xml. It scans src/site/markdown for @guidance comments and excludes generated target content.

examples.title: Configure the plugin in pom.xml and run short goals
examples.description: Add the plugin to the Maven build to enable short goal names such as gw:gw and gw:act. The configuration selects the model, server credentials id, default scan path, and instructions file.

examples.title: Run a predefined act or prompt-only act
commands: mvn gw:act -Dgw.act=">Update the project documentation for the latest release" -Dgw.path=src/site/markdown
examples.description: Use gw:act when you want to apply a reusable act or a one-off prompt. A predefined act is passed by name, while direct user prompt mode starts with the > character.

examples.title: Process a multi-module Maven reactor per module
examples.description: Use gw:gw-per-module when each module should be handled by Maven's standard reactor lifecycle. The command can be combined with Maven parallel execution and module-specific scan paths.

examples.title: Enable focused debug logging
examples.description: Use SLF4J SimpleLogger properties to troubleshoot plugin execution for a package or fully qualified class. Replace DEBUG with TRACE, INFO, WARN, or ERROR as needed.
